chunks: And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Everything in the human body that exists in pairs carries the full blood money (diyyah) for both, and half the blood money for one of them. And whatever exists as a single part carries the full blood money.

key_terms.فِي ٱلْإِنْسَانِ: in the human body; indicating the ruling concerns bodily members
key_terms.نِصْفُ ٱلدِّيَةِ: half of the blood money; the compensation for one of a paired set
key_terms.وَاحِدًا: single; a body part that exists only once in the body
key_terms.ٱثْنَيْنِ: a pair; body parts that naturally come in twos
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: blood money; the prescribed financial compensation for bodily injury or loss

ai.seo_question: How is diyyah calculated for paired and single body parts in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a general fiqh principle for bodily injury compensation. If a body part exists as a pair, the full diyyah applies to both together and half applies to one; if it is a single organ or part, its loss entails the full diyyah.
